name: Corvo Ride Hailing
note: Routes are real shortest paths: Dijkstra over a jittered street graph with a river and three bridges, so the distance, minutes, fare lines (which sum to the total) and pickup ETAs all come from the same route, and the assigned car follows it with a smoothed heading on a rAF loop that pauses off screen. Pan by dragging, tap to drop a pin, and the viewBox eases to fit each route. Set --amo-ride-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Stopwise Courier Route
note: Northside is a street grid laid at -20 degrees, so every leg is a real two-street drive and the drawn route, the kilometres, the turn-by-turn steps and the window-aware ETAs all come from that one L-shaped leg. Stops reorder by pointer drag on a fixed-pitch list, Alt+arrows or Optimise (nearest neighbour, then 2-opt and relocate passes against a lateness-weighted cost), each move FLIP-animated and undoable, and proof of delivery is a DPR-aware signature canvas. Set --amo-courier-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Meridian Journey Planner
note: A small RAPTOR search over five headway timetables with today's delays, change times, walking links and a step-free rule: each round that improves the arrival is one more change, and re-running just after the earliest boarding yields later departures. The options share one time axis so their segment bars compare at a glance, and the network diagram redraws the chosen path with a pathLength dash animation. Set --amo-transit-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Wisp Scooter Rental
note: Zones are polygons and every rule is a point-in-polygon test on the live position: the Old Town caps speed at 10 km/h and End ride only unlocks inside a parking bay. Unlocking is press-and-hold, its ring a conic-gradient driven by a registered angle @property, and a 20x ride clock runs in a rAF loop that pauses off screen, integrating fare, distance and battery from the same movement. Set --amo-scoot-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Bayfinder Parking
note: The rotary duration dial is a role=slider whose arc and knob are both driven by one registered angle @property, so keyboard steps glide while dragging tracks the pointer; each car park's tariff (stepped hours, bands, daily caps, maximum stays) feeds the dial price, the itemised lines and the end-of-session charge from one function. Floor plans are generated per level from a seeded PRNG, and the list's free counts are counted from those bays. Set --amo-park-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Relay Dispatch Board
note: Pointer-driven drag scheduling on a Gantt that snaps to 15 minutes: the preview block validates live, hard rules (vehicle class, weight, shift, jobs already underway) refuse the drop with a reason and soft rules (overlap, outside the window) flag a conflict the header counts. Greedy auto-assign with a travel buffer, keyboard moves, an undo/redo snapshot stack and a Web Animations FLIP for every block that moves. Set --amo-dispatch-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Cubby Parcel Locker
note: The wall is a CSS grid where each door spans the rows its size needs, and every door is a compartment plus a hinged leaf with its own perspective, updated in place so the rotateY swing transitions both ways. Codes from the phone panel or the keypad (keyboard digits work too) open the right doors in turn, three misses lock the keypad for 30 seconds, and returns pick the best free door, preferring seated reach when Lower doors is on. Set --amo-locker-h to 100dvh in an app.
html: CubbyLinden Street · Locker 0417

name: Odo Fleet Maintenance
note: Every service interval is kilometres or months, whichever comes first, with the kilometre side projected into a date from the vehicle's own km a day since its last service, so the status, both meters, the due date and the due-first badge share one calculation. Logging work (a validated form with live totals) resets the interval and lands in its month on a stacked CSS bar chart whose breakdown always sums to the bar, and every log or removal can be undone. Set --amo-fleet-h to 100dvh in an app.
